A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Optimist routing work. The text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark recall comparisons, parameter sweeps, covariance analyses, and maximum-inner-product prediction errors.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark analyses and adds query-latency experiments and router-size results.

M1.justification: Equations (5) and (7) and Algorithm 1 retain the same mean/covariance scoring rule, diagonal-plus-low-rank sketch, and shard selection procedure. The name 'Masked Sketch' and rewritten pseudocode describe the existing method.

E1.justification: The same six datasets, embedding representations, and MIPS tasks remain. v2 additionally evaluates retrieval with shards stored on SSD and blob storage, extending the tested operational environments beyond v1's recall-versus-points experiments.

E2.justification: Mean, NormalizedMean, Scann, and SubPartition remain in the main comparisons. However, SubPartition is removed from the optimism-parameter sweep: it appears in v1 Figure 10 but is absent from the corresponding v2 Figures 6 and 14.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a substantial latency-evaluation protocol at 95% recall, separating routing, fetching, and scoring, using PQ with four-dimensional codebooks and testing 1, 2, and 4 threads on SSD and blob storage. The existing exact-scan recall protocol remains; relabeling accuracy as recall does not change that metric.

E4.justification: v2 adds latency decomposition and thread-count sensitivity analysis in Figures 4 and 12. The covariance-rank, optimism, and prediction-error analyses are largely retained and redistributed, although the optimism sweep loses its direct SubPartition comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The new timing means and P50 summaries do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds latency and router-size results. For example, Figure 4 reports Music latency reductions of 46.51% on SSD and 54.96% on blob storage versus NormalizedMean with four threads. v1 Table 1's DeepImage zeros are replaced by prose reporting 9% and 10% more points at 90% and 95% recall. Other savings entries remain unchanged. The NQ-Ada2 spherical-KMeans top-10 results shown in v1 Figures 2 and 6 are omitted from v2.

T1.justification: Lemma 2 relaxes the normalized-covariance eigenvalue threshold from 2 to 1, with a revised proof in v2 Appendix B. Section 2.2 also replaces the claimed mean-only limit as delta approaches zero with the maximum of mean and median scores. These are substantive but limited refinements of the existing analysis.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a moments-based optimistic router, a compact covariance sketch, and comparable recall while probing up to 50% fewer points. Suitability for high-latency external storage was already claimed in v1; the new latency experiments support that retained claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds a speculative explanation linking DeepImage's shortfall to its PCA-based representation. It also specifies how bandwidth, thread availability, compression, and scoring speed affect latency benefits, and expands the explanation of routing/scoring independence. These sharpen the existing applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v1 only promises a future code release; v2 states that Rust code and experimental configurations are open-sourced and supplies a repository link. v2 also discloses exact partition counts and the new experiments' AWS machine, memory, bandwidth, compression, and thread settings, substantially improving reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds footnoted references to Turbopuffer and Pinecone serverless architectures to connect the work to deployed storage-backed vector systems. The scholarly bibliography and positioning relative to existing routing research remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises the introduction, method exposition, and conclusion, adds an illustrative-example subsection, and changes 'search' terminology to 'scoring.' Dataset descriptions and parameter discussions move into the main text, while method subsections and appendices are reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ACM layout and substantially rearranges displays. It adds a dataset/configuration table and latency charts, expands Figure 3, reduces Figure 2 to two panels, moves parameter and full prediction-error displays into the main text, and changes plot labels from accuracy to recall. The savings table also loses its DeepImage column.

improvement.justification: v1 primarily supports efficiency through points probed despite Optimist's extra routing computation. v2 directly tests this central practical tradeoff through routing/fetch/scoring latency, storage and thread comparisons, and concrete router sizes, including unfavorable outcomes. Added configuration and code-access information further strengthens the paper. The omitted NQ-Ada2 top-10 results and SubPartition sweep comparison are limited setbacks relative to these substantial gains.
